basic_info.name: Sofia Crespo / Entangled Others
basic_info.active_years: 2018-present (Sofia Crespo solo from ~2017; Entangled Others studio with Feileacan McCormick from ~2020)
basic_info.location: Lisbon, Portugal (previously Berlin, Germany; Buenos Aires, Argentina)

practice_description.medium: AI-generated imagery, generative video, interactive installation, NFT art, bio-digital art
practice_description.practice_summary: Sofia Crespo and Feileacan McCormick (as Entangled Others) create neural network-generated organisms and ecosystems that explore more-than-human relationships, using machine learning to imagine hybrid life forms, speculative ecologies, and interspecies entanglements that challenge anthropocentric perspectives on nature and intelligence.
practice_description.methodology: The practice involves training neural networks (GANs, diffusion models, custom architectures) on datasets of biological imagery — deep sea organisms, microscopic life, coral formations, fungi, botanical specimens. Rather than pursuing photorealism, they train models to generate uncanny hybrid organisms that exist between categories — part jellyfish, part flower, part something entirely new. The training data curation is an artistic act: selecting which organisms and ecosystems to train on shapes the aesthetic and conceptual territory of the output. Recent work under the Entangled Others banner has expanded to include real-time generative ecosystems, AR installations, and interactive works that respond to environmental data (coral bleaching data, biodiversity metrics). They combine outputs from multiple model architectures and post-process results to create coherent visual worlds.

relevance_to_sense_room.relevance_summary: Crespo/Entangled Others demonstrate how neural networks can generate living ecosystemic compositions — visual worlds where organisms relate to each other and their environment. Their work models how A(DAI)'s knowledge graph could manifest as a living ecology of connected entities rather than a static map, with the relational and more-than-human frameworks directly relevant to the Sense Room's ethos.
relevance_to_sense_room.art_as_substrate: Yes. The generated organisms and ecosystems function as a living visual substrate — a continuously evolving ecology that fills the visual field. Works like Artificial Natural History create entire taxonomies of speculative life that serve as ambient, generative environments rather than discrete objects.
relevance_to_sense_room.relational_composition: Yes. The ecosystemic framework is inherently relational — organisms exist in relationship to each other and to their environment. Recent interactive works create simulated ecosystems where entities interact, compete, and cooperate based on relational rules. The 'entangled' in the studio name signals the primacy of relationships over individual entities.
relevance_to_sense_room.self_recomposing: Yes. Generative works continuously produce new organisms and configurations. Interactive ecosystem simulations evolve over time as entities interact. When connected to environmental data (e.g., real-time coral bleaching metrics), the visual ecosystem responds to changes in the living world.

works.title: Artificial Natural History
works.description: A series of GAN-generated organisms that form a speculative taxonomy of non-existent life — creatures that sit between known biological categories, generated by training neural networks on diverse biological imagery. Presented as prints, video, and interactive explorations of the latent space of imagined biology.
works.relevance: Demonstrates the concept of a generative taxonomy — an AI-produced catalogue of entities defined by their relationships to each other. Directly analogous to how A(DAI) could generate relational maps of the digital arts field.

works.title: Beneath the Neural Waves
works.description: An immersive generative video work depicting an AI-imagined deep sea ecosystem. Neural networks trained on deep ocean organism footage generate continuously evolving underwater landscapes populated by speculative creatures. Shown as large-scale projection installation.
works.relevance: Models an immersive ecosystem generated from trained neural networks — a living environment that visitors can dwell within. Demonstrates how generative AI can produce coherent, relational visual worlds.

works.title: A Study of Entanglement
works.description: Interactive installation by Entangled Others exploring interspecies relationships through real-time generative visuals. Organisms generated by AI models interact with each other on screen, forming and dissolving relationships. Connected to environmental data to reflect real-world ecological conditions.
works.relevance: The most directly relevant work — a generative relational ecosystem that responds to real-world data. Models exactly what A(DAI)'s Sense Room could look like: a living ecology of entities whose relationships are visible, dynamic, and data-driven.

protocol_art_resonance.protocol_art_summary: The practice treats the design of training pipelines, dataset curation protocols, and ecosystem simulation rules as creative acts. The decision of which organisms to include in training data, how models are combined, and what rules govern ecosystemic interactions are protocol-level artistic decisions. The Entangled Others studio is itself a protocol for collaborative more-than-human creative practice.
protocol_art_resonance.system_designed: Custom neural network training pipelines for biological imagery generation. Ecosystem simulation frameworks for interactive installations. The Entangled Others studio model itself — a framework for collaborative practice focused on more-than-human relationships.

commons_orientation.commons_summary: Active participants in the open/decentralised art ecosystem — significant presence on platforms like Tezos/fxhash and Feral File that emphasise artist-accessible, lower-barrier models. Some tools and techniques shared through talks, workshops, and process documentation. However, specific trained models and software are not formally open-sourced. NFT sales provide primary revenue. The practice is philosophically aligned with commons values (ecological thinking, shared planetary futures) but economically operates within art market structures.

governance_model.governance_detail: Entangled Others is a two-person studio partnership between Sofia Crespo and Feileacan McCormick, with shared creative direction. Decisions are collaborative. Earlier solo work by Crespo was individually governed. Project-specific collaborations with scientists and ecologists involve domain expertise but the studio retains creative control.

consent_and_authorship.consent_approach: Training data is sourced from biological imagery — photographs and videos of non-human organisms. No consent issues with human subjects. However, the practice raises interesting questions about consent in relation to non-human life — the 'entangled others' framework implicitly asks what it means to represent other species through AI systems trained on human-captured imagery of them.
consent_and_authorship.authorship_model: Collaborative — shared authorship between Crespo and McCormick as Entangled Others. Machine co-authorship is implicit in the generative process — the neural networks produce the organisms, but the artists curate the training data, design the systems, and select/compose the outputs. The more-than-human framing extends the question of authorship beyond human agents.

liveness_and_duration.temporal_detail: Generative works continuously produce new organisms and configurations. Interactive ecosystem simulations evolve as entities interact according to designed rules. When connected to environmental data feeds, the visual ecology reflects real-world ecological changes over time. The systems are designed to run indefinitely without repeating.

data_materiality.data_sources: Biological photography and video: deep sea organisms, coral reefs, microscopic life, fungi, botanical specimens, entomological collections. Museum natural history collections. Scientific imaging datasets. Real-time environmental data (coral bleaching indices, biodiversity metrics) for data-responsive works.
data_materiality.data_provenance: Mixed. Training imagery sourced from publicly available scientific datasets, natural history museum digital collections, web-scraped biological photography, and self-collected footage. Environmental data from open scientific databases. The provenance is acknowledged but not always exhaustively documented. No personal human data is used.

embedding_space_relevance.embedding_summary: Significant engagement. The practice navigates GAN latent spaces to discover hybrid organisms that exist between biological categories — the latent space of a model trained on biological imagery becomes a space of speculative biology. Traversing this space reveals unexpected morphological connections between species. The latent space functions as a space of potential life forms.
embedding_space_relevance.multimodal: Primarily visual, but expanding. Recent work incorporates sound design for immersive installations and real-time environmental data integration. The conceptual framework is inherently multimodal (visual organisms in sonic environments responding to ecological data) but the AI generation is primarily image-based.

exhibition_modality.spatial_description: Works manifest as large-scale projection installations (immersive ecosystem environments), screen-based generative video, high-resolution prints and NFTs, and interactive installations with environmental data integration. Exhibition contexts range from galleries and museums to digital art platforms (fxhash, Feral File). The immersive installations create room-scale environments where generated organisms surround viewers.

interoperability.composability: Generative outputs (images, video streams) could theoretically serve as inputs to other systems. The ecosystem simulation frameworks could incorporate external data feeds. However, current works are self-contained and do not expose APIs or standard interfaces for external integration.
interoperability.technical_openness: Partially open. Process and methodology are shared through talks and documentation. Specific software and trained models are not formally open-sourced. The practice is communicative about methods but protective of specific implementations.

technical_approach.stack: Python, PyTorch/TensorFlow for neural network training, StyleGAN2/3 and custom GAN architectures, diffusion models, custom ecosystem simulation code, TouchDesigner for real-time interactive installations, Unreal Engine for some immersive works, environmental data APIs for data-responsive pieces.

network_position.scene_affiliation: AI art, bio-digital art, generative art, NFT/crypto art (Tezos/fxhash ecosystem), ecological art, more-than-human design. Connected to both the crypto-native generative art community and the institutional contemporary art world. Active in the Tezos generative art scene and Feral File platform. Bridges art, ecology, and technology communities.
network_position.connections: Mario Klingemann (both GAN art pioneers, but Crespo focused on biological/ecological aesthetics while Klingemann explores human portraiture and abstract aesthetics). Refik Anadol (both create AI-generated immersive environments, but Entangled Others' work is ecologically oriented rather than data-spectacle). Casey Reas (connected through generative art and Art Blocks/fxhash communities). Philip Beesley (shared interest in more-than-human relational systems, but from physical-architectural vs. neural-network perspectives).

potential_role_in_adai.role_detail: Entangled Others brings: (1) a working model for how AI-generated ecosystems can function as relational, evolving environments — directly applicable to the Sense Room, (2) more-than-human frameworks that align with A(DAI)'s interest in expanding beyond anthropocentric intelligence, (3) practical expertise in connecting generative systems to real-world ecological data, (4) experience navigating both crypto-native and institutional art contexts. Their ecosystemic approach to AI art is the closest existing practice to what A(DAI)'s graph-curated Sense Room envisions.
